battle.name: 十二月黨人起義
battle.brief: 1825 年 12 月 26 日，亞歷山大一世病逝，北方社率近衛軍團與海軍船團約三千人集結元老院廣場，拒絕向尼古拉一世宣誓，釀成一日政變。卡面這件輪發手槍象徵近衛與火槍隊軍官才配得上的昂貴副武器譜系；當日短火器已是燧發式，扭轉局面的卻是三門裝葡萄彈的野戰砲。

kit.name: 輪發手槍
kit.history: 最早的後膛手槍。機械太貴，只給火槍隊的軍官與近衛。

countries: 起義爆發於 1825 年 12 月 26 日（俄曆 12 月 14 日）的聖彼得堡元老院廣場，交戰雙方都出自俄羅斯帝國本身的建制，並非對外戰爭。叛方是北方社為核心的近衛軍官與士兵聯盟，實際投入的部隊包括近衛莫斯科團的部分連隊、近衛擲彈兵團的部分連隊，以及近衛海軍船團的水兵營，投入兵力約三千人；社內推舉普林策·謝爾蓋耶維奇·特魯布茨科伊為臨時執政者，政治藍圖則是尼基塔·穆拉維約夫起草、參照美國憲法寫成的君主立憲綱要，主張廢除農奴制但保留地主土地，設立法議會，不要求推翻皇室。以佩斯捷爾為首、駐在烏克蘭土爾琴的南方社主張共和並把土地一半收歸國家；聯合斯拉夫人團體則主張俄羅斯與波蘭、匈牙利等斯拉夫民族組成平等聯邦。忠方是剛於 12 月 1 日（俄曆 11 月 19 日）迎來亞歷山大一世病逝、隨即由尼古拉一世繼位的新皇權力中樞：皇帝本人親臨廣場主持效忠宣誓，御前會議與內務部警察控制市區街道，近衛騎士團（馬里亞·費奧多羅芙娜皇太后御用的騎兵營）負責騎兵衝鋒，御前近衛步兵與炮兵封鎖元老院四周出入要道，警察與忠誠守軍夜間搜查全城。集結在廣場周邊的忠誠部隊約九千人，編制上仍屬帝國常備軍，只是拒絕響應叛軍的召集。南方戰線由帝國地方當局與平叛部隊應對：烏克蘭切爾尼戈夫團的起義由謝爾蓋·穆拉維約夫-阿波斯托爾率領，因平叛軍配備大量火砲而優勢懸殊，僅五日即被壓制，與其事有關者逾三千人被捕。
countriesEn: The revolt broke out on 26 December 1825 (14 December Old Style) in Senate Square, Saint Petersburg, and both sides came from inside the institutions of the Russian Empire itself rather than from any external war. The rebel side was an alliance of guards officers and enlisted men centred on the Northern Society; the troops actually committed were elements of the Life-Guards Moscow Regiment, elements of the Grenadier Life Guards Regiment, and the Naval Equipage of the Guard, together some three thousand men. The society nominated Prince Sergei Pavlovich Trubetskoy as interim ruler, and its political programme was the constitutional charter drawn up by Nikita Muravyov on the model of the United States Constitution: abolition of serfdom with the land retained by the landowners, a legislative assembly, and no demand to abolish the imperial house. The Southern Society under Pavel Pestel, based at Tulchin in Ukraine, wanted a republic with half the land taken into state ownership, while the Society of United Slavs called for an equal federation of Russia with Poland, Hungary and the other Slavic nations. The loyal side was the new imperial power centre under Nicholas I, who had taken the throne after the death of Alexander I on 1 December (19 November Old Style): the emperor appeared in person at the square to preside over the oath, the State Council and the Ministry of Internal Affairs police controlled the streets of the capital, the Chevalier Guard Regiment of Empress Maria Theodorovna provided the cavalry, and the imperial guards infantry with the artillery sealed the approaches to the Senate, while police and loyal garrison units searched the city at night. The loyal troops massed around the square numbered about nine thousand; in establishment terms they were still ordinary imperial units that simply refused to answer the rebels' summons. On the southern front the empire's provincial authorities and the columns sent against the insurgents met the Chernigov Regiment revolt led by Sergey Muravyov-Apostol. The rebels were outmatched by a force that brought a large train of artillery, the rising was crushed within five days, and more than three thousand people connected with it were taken into custody.
people: 關鍵人物集中在交接王位的那幾日。亞歷山大一世於 12 月 1 日（俄曆 11 月 19 日）在彼得霍夫離世，遺下兩個弟弟康斯坦丁與尼古拉；康斯坦丁其實早在 1823 年已秘密放棄繼承權，但宮廷與公眾都不知情，於是部分近衛軍在 12 月初誤向康斯坦丁宣誓效忠，12 月 26 日原定向尼古拉一世宣誓的儀式因此充滿疑慮，這正是北方社決定當日動手的直接契機。叛方領袖層在起義當日就失去重心：被推舉的臨時執政者特魯布茨科伊缺席廣場，其副手布拉托夫上校同樣不知去向，軍官們倉促改推歐根·奧博列恩斯基公爵接手指揮；起草並公開宣讀起義聲明的正是奧博列恩斯基。樞密院元帥米哈伊爾·米洛拉多維奇奉尼古拉一世之命到廣場勸降，在公眾面前發言時被後排的彼得·卡霍夫斯基從背後開槍擊中，隨即又被奧博列恩斯基以刺刀刺中而當場身亡。另有一支以帕諾夫中尉為首的擲彈兵小分隊衝入冬宮，企圖奪取宮中權柄，失敗後退回廣場。南方社領袖佩斯捷爾在起義前一天（俄曆 12 月 13 日、新曆 25 日）即被警方以叛國罪名拘捕，社內兩週後才得知首都的消息；接掌烏克蘭起義的穆拉維約夫-阿波斯托爾隨後率切爾尼戈夫團與瓦西爾基夫駐軍響應。事後清算時，五名首要人物被判死刑，其中一人在行刑前身故，其餘四人於 1826 年 7 月被公開絞刑；秘密結社的骨幹則被分批流放西伯利亞，接受特別法庭的審判與軍事懲罰。
peopleEn: The decisive figures cluster around the few days in which the succession was settled. Alexander I died at Peterhof on 1 December (19 November Old Style), leaving two brothers, Konstantin and Nicholas. Konstantin had in fact renounced his claim in secret as early as 1823, but neither the court nor the public knew this, so part of the guards had already sworn loyalty to Konstantin in early December. The oath scheduled for 26 December before Nicholas I was therefore surrounded with suspicion, and that ambiguity was the immediate occasion for the Northern Society to move on that very day. The rebel leadership lost its centre on the morning of the rising: Trubetskoy, the nominated interim ruler, failed to appear in the square, and his second-in-command, Colonel Bulatov, likewise went missing, so the officers hastily appointed Prince Eugene Obolensky to take command. Obolensky was also the man who drew up and publicly read out the rebels' declaration. Field Marshal Mikhail Miloradovich was sent by Nicholas I to parley with the insurgents; while delivering a public address he was shot in the back by Pyotr Kakhovsky, firing from the ranks behind him, and was then stabbed by Obolensky, dying on the spot. At the same moment a rebel grenadier squad led by Lieutenant Nikolay Panov entered the Winter Palace in an attempt to seize power at court, failed, and withdrew back to the square. On the southern side Pavel Pestel, the leading figure of the Southern Society, was arrested by the police on a charge of treason the day before the rising (13 December Old Style, 25 December New Style), and the society itself only learned what had happened in the capital two weeks later. Sergey Muravyov-Apostol, who took charge of the Ukrainian rising, then led the Chernigov Regiment and the garrison at Vasilkov in answer to it. In the reckoning that followed, five principal leaders were sentenced to death; one died before the execution could be carried out, and the remaining four were publicly hanged in July 1826. The backbone of the secret societies was meanwhile shipped off to Siberia in batches, to face special commissions and military punishment.
kits: 卡面這件輪發手槍是十六世紀初在德意志與西班牙一帶流傳的後膛手槍，機械結構昂貴，所以只配發給火槍隊的軍官與近衛，成為軍階與近衛身分的直接標記；到 1825 年，這種以機械發條運作的機構早已被燧發式取代，軍械庫裡流通的官用手槍都是燧發槍，輪發手槍只剩少數作為古董與工藝品流傳。換言之，十二月黨人起義當日雙方軍官插在腰間的短火器，技術上已是卡面武器的後代而非本體；卡面之器在此代表的，正是那條「近衛與火槍隊軍官才配得上的昂貴個人副武器」譜系的起點。實際投入交火的裝備包括：叛軍一側以近衛步軍的燧發滑膛步槍為主，配俄式刺刀與皮製裝備，海軍船團的水兵另用斧與劍；近衛騎士團裝騎兵卡賓槍與彎刀，配鞍具與馬刺；帕諾夫小分隊衝進冬宮時攜帶的是短兵與火槍。決定局面的則是炮兵：日暮時皇帝下令以三門野戰砲發射葡萄彈，對廣場上密集列隊的叛軍造成毀滅性衝擊，部分退向結冰涅瓦河的叛軍再次遭到射擊，冰面被轟碎。另外值得記錄的是 1820 年謝苗諾夫斯基近衛團的士兵起義，當時他們能以刺刀完成襲擊，說明這類變亂所依賴的不是火器優勢，而是軍隊內部效忠的轉向；這一點在評估本次雙方裝備差距時特別重要。
kitsEn: The wheellock pistol on the card is a breech-loading handgun that circulated in Germany and Spain from the early sixteenth century. Its mechanism was expensive, so it was issued only to officers of the musket line and to the guards, and it served as a direct mark of rank and of guard status. By 1825 the mechanism, driven by a mechanical spring, had long been superseded by the flintlock; the officer pistols in the arsenals were flintlocks, and only a few wheellocks survived as antiques and collectors' pieces. In other words, the short guns carried in the belts of officers on both sides during the Decembrist rising were technically descendants of the weapon on the card rather than the weapon itself. What the card stands for is the beginning of that line of expensive personal sidearms reserved for guardsmen and officers of the musket line. The equipment actually used in the fighting was as follows. On the rebel side the base was the flintlock smoothbore musket of the guards infantry, with Russian bayonets and leather kit; the men of the Naval Equipage of the Guard also carried axes and swords. The Chevalier Guard Regiment carried cavalry carbines and sabres, with saddles and spurs. Panov's grenadier squad took short weapons and muskets when it pushed into the Winter Palace. What decided the issue was the artillery: at dusk the emperor ordered three field guns to fire grapeshot, and the effect on the densely ranked rebels in the square was devastating; those who retreated north towards the frozen Neva were shelled again, and the ice was broken up by the impact. It is also worth recording the mutiny of the soldiers of the Life-Guards Semeonovsky Regiment in 1820, when an assault was carried out with bayonets alone. That episode shows that such disturbances of the military order did not rest on any advantage in firearms, but on a shift of loyalty inside the ranks, and that point matters greatly when weighing the equipment gap between the two sides in 1825.
tactics: 叛軍的戰術建立在政治算計而非野戰能力上：北方社原本計畫在 1826 年與南方社同時行動，亞歷山大一世猝死迫使他們提前，把目標定在 12 月 26 日尼古拉一世向元老院宣誓的那一刻，只要近衛軍拒絕宣誓並轉而擁護康斯坦丁，帝國權力中樞就會在不流血的情況下易手。因此起義者集結在元老院廣場而不是任何城門或軍營門口，企圖以拒絕儀式製造既成事實，再吸納更多團隊與駐軍倒戈。實際執行卻漏洞百出：特魯布茨科伊與布拉托夫先後缺席，臨場指揮真空使決策反覆；只有約三千人到場，其餘駐紮部隊按兵不動；叛軍沒有攻擊元老院本身，只以零星射擊與口頭聲明維持陣線。米洛拉多維奇被殺之後，忠方沒有立刻還手，而是繼續談判整個白日，同時把忠誠部隊向廣場收攏，把時間用在等待而非進攻。騎兵衝鋒由近衛騎士團執行，騎士團在結冰的鵝卵石上打滑，衝鋒一度潰散。真正解決僵局的是傍晚皇帝親自下令的三門砲齊射：葡萄彈在密集人羣中造成毀滅性效果，叛軍當場潰散，部分人向北退往結冰的涅瓦河企圖重組，卻再度遭到炮擊，冰面被擊碎。南方戰線的起義同樣沒有攻勢計劃：切爾尼戈夫團與瓦西爾基夫駐軍短時間內控制當地，但平叛部隊以大量火砲和優勢兵力壓上，起義在五天內被解除。同一套邏輯貫穿南北：北方敗在沒有砲，南方敗在對方有砲。
tacticsEn: The tactics of the rebels rested on political calculation rather than on any capacity for field fighting. The Northern Society had originally planned joint action with the Southern Society in 1826; the sudden death of Alexander I forced their hand and fixed their target on 26 December, the moment Nicholas I was to take the oath in the Senate. If the guards refused the oath and transferred their allegiance to Konstantin, the centre of imperial power would change hands without blood being shed. The insurgents accordingly massed in Senate Square rather than at any city gate or barracks entrance, hoping to create a fait accompli by refusing the ceremony and then to draw further regiments and garrisons over to their side. In execution the plan was full of holes: Trubetskoy and Bulatov were both absent, and the resulting vacuum in command produced repeated changes of decision; only about three thousand men came, the rest of the garrison stood still, and the rebels never assaulted the Senate itself, holding their line with scattered firing and spoken declarations. After Miloradovich was killed the loyal side did not return fire at once but kept talking for the whole day, drawing the loyal units in towards the square, spending time on waiting rather than on attacking. The cavalry charge was entrusted to the Chevalier Guard Regiment, which slipped on the icy cobbles and the charge broke up in disorder. What actually broke the stalemate was the evening salvo of three guns ordered by the emperor in person: grapeshot into a densely packed body of men had a devastating effect, the rebels broke and ran, and those who withdrew north towards the frozen Neva in an attempt to re-form were shelled again, the ice breaking under the impact. The southern rising was no more offensive in plan: the Chernigov Regiment and the Vasilkov garrison controlled the town for a short time, but columns with a heavy weight of artillery and superior numbers pressed in and the revolt was put down within five days. The same logic runs through both ends of the revolt: the north lacked guns, and the south faced an enemy who had them.
data: 可核對的數字集中在兵力和司法兩個層面。起義當日叛軍投入約三千人，來自近衛莫斯科團、近衛擲彈兵團的部分連隊與近衛海軍船團；忠誠部隊在元老院周圍約九千人，雙方在廣場形成僵持；近衛騎士團一個騎兵營奉命衝鋒；日暮時投入射擊的是三門野戰砲，彈藥為葡萄彈。整場起義在首都只延續一日，冬宮未被奪取。司法與懲罰的數字有完整記錄：北方社受審者六十一人，南方社三十七人，聯合斯拉夫人二十三人；死刑判決包括判肢解刑者五人與判斬首者三十一人，另有十七人革職除籍、十六人終身苦役流放、五人苦役流放十年、十五人苦役流放六年、十五人流放居住地，其餘為降為列兵或撤銷官階與貴族身分；五名首要人物原判死刑，改判後其中一人在行刑前身故，其餘四人於 1826 年 7 月在西伯利亞流放起程之前被公開絞刑。士兵與團體方面，秘密結社成員約一百二十人遭受獄中羈押、降職、調往高加索軍區或警察監視等法外處分；由特別委員會審理的士兵案件中，一百七十八人受鞭刑，另有二十三人受其他肉刑；其餘約四千名士兵被編成混成近衛團，調往高加索作戰區。另有先由特別委員會審理的一批黨人共一百二十四人，其中十五人被最高刑庭判為流放居住地，送往別列佐沃、納雷姆、蘇爾古特等北亞地帶；首批流放者於 1826 年 7 月 13 日（俄曆）起程前往尼爾琴斯克礦區，最大一批先安置於奇塔，三年後再轉往尼爾琴斯克附近的彼得羅夫斯基鑄造廠，多數在 1835 至 1837 年間離開。
dataEn: The verifiable figures fall into two groups, force strengths and sentences. On the day of the rising the rebels committed about three thousand men drawn from the Life-Guards Moscow Regiment, elements of the Grenadier Life Guards Regiment and the Naval Equipage of the Guard; the loyal troops around the Senate numbered about nine thousand, and the two sides stood in a stalemate in the square. One cavalry regiment of the Chevalier Guard was ordered to charge, and at dusk the shooting was done by three field guns firing grapeshot. The rising lasted a single day in the capital, and the Winter Palace was never taken. The judicial record is complete. Sixty-one men of the Northern Society, thirty-seven of the Southern Society and twenty-three of the United Slavs were brought to trial. Death sentences included five by quartering and thirty-one by beheading; seventeen were cashiered and stripped of rank, sixteen were sentenced to lifelong exile with hard labour, five to exile with hard labour for ten years, fifteen to six years, fifteen to exile by settlement, and the rest were demoted to soldier or deprived of rank and nobility. The five principal leaders had originally been condemned to death; after commutation one of them died before the execution, and the other four were publicly hanged in July 1826, before the first convoys set out for Siberia. On the collective side, about one hundred and twenty members of the secret societies underwent extrajudicial repression: imprisonment in fortress, demotion, transfer to the Caucasus, or police supervision. In the cases of enlisted soldiers examined by special commissions, one hundred and seventy-eight were sentenced to the gauntlet and another twenty-three to other corporal punishments; the remaining men, roughly four thousand, were formed into a combined guards regiment and sent to the Caucasian theatre of operations. A further batch of one hundred and twenty-four members had been examined by a special commission, of whom fifteen were convicted of state crimes by the Supreme Criminal Court and sentenced to exile by settlement in places such as Berezov, Narym and Surgut. The first convoy set out for the Nerchinsk mining district on 13 July 1826 (Old Style); the largest group was settled first at Chita and transferred three years later to Petrovsky Zavod near Nerchinsk, most of them leaving between 1835 and 1837.
cause: 起義的直接導火線是 1825 年 12 月 1 日（俄曆 11 月 19 日）亞歷山大一世在彼得霍夫突然病逝，留下的王位交接本身充滿含糊：康斯坦丁公爵早在 1823 年已私下放棄繼承，但消息未公開，宮廷只得以一場對康斯坦丁的效忠儀式作為過渡，而 12 月 26 日預定舉行的向尼古拉一世宣誓因此被視為篡位的確認，北方社遂利用這個空檔武裝起事。更深的成因是亞歷山大一世的改革及其反覆：1815 至 1821 年間，帝國在官僚與教育制度上進行過自由化試驗，內務大臣斯佩蘭斯基整頓行政，1818 年更曾命人起草憲法，但拿破崙戰爭的衝擊使朝廷把一切言論自由都視為法國式動亂的源頭，改革全面回頭，警察與審查制度收緊，改革派軍官普遍感到被出賣。再往下是農奴制與邊疆問題：1816 至 1819 年波羅的海省份已廢除農奴制，內陸各省的農奴起義此起彼伏，白俄羅斯與立陶宛的軍中平民起義、西部邊疆軍隊的騷動，讓軍官看到軍隊本身並不可靠。1820 年謝苗諾夫斯基近衛團士兵起義以刺刀襲擊的方式爆發，成為秘密結社分裂為南北兩社的直接刺激，1821 年社務一度中止，1823 年成立聯合斯拉夫人團體，1825 年 9 月兩社在瓦西爾基夫召開聯席會議，才又把武裝行動排入日程。
causeEn: The immediate trigger was the sudden death of Alexander I at Peterhof on 1 December 1825 (19 November Old Style), and the succession he left behind was itself full of ambiguity. Konstantin had renounced the throne in private as early as 1823, but the fact was not public, so the court could only manage the transition with a ceremony of allegiance to Konstantin; the oath to Nicholas I scheduled for 26 December was therefore read as the confirmation of a usurpation, and the Northern Society used that gap to rise in arms. Beneath the trigger lay the reform movement under Alexander I and its reversal. Between 1815 and 1821 the empire had experimented with liberalising its bureaucracy and its system of education, with Speransky reorganising the Ministry of the Interior and an order for the drafting of a constitution in 1818; but the shock of the Napoleonic Wars convinced the court that all freedom of speech was the fountainhead of French-style disorder, the reforms were abandoned, policing and censorship tightened, and reformist officers came to feel themselves betrayed. Underneath that lay serfdom and the frontier question: serfdom had been abolished in the Baltic provinces between 1816 and 1819, peasant risings broke out repeatedly in the interior provinces, and mutinies of conscript soldiers in Belorussia, Lithuania and the western borderlands taught officers that the army itself could not be relied upon. The mutiny of the soldiers of the Life-Guards Semeonovsky Regiment in 1820, carried out with bayonets, was the direct shock that split the secret societies into a Northern and a Southern Society; activity was suspended in 1821, the Society of United Slavs was founded in 1823, and only the joint council at Vasilkov in September 1825 put an armed action back on the programme.
impact: 起義在當日就被壓平，但它留下的裂縫延續了半個世紀。尼古拉一世保住王位之後的反應不是開明而是收縮：秘密結社骨幹被大批流放到尼爾琴斯克、奇塔、彼得羅夫斯基鑄造廠等西伯利亞據點，帝國設立由別肯多夫伯爵主持的第三廳專門監視國內政治異議，軍隊內部進行大規模清剿，約四千名士兵被編為混成近衛團派往高加索作戰區，參與 1828 至 1829 年的俄土戰爭以及對高加索山民的戰役，這批人在往後成為各類兵變與十二月黨人敘事的象徵。流放者本身則改變了東向的邊陲：奇塔與彼得羅夫斯基鑄造廠聚集了數十名受過軍事與高等教育的前近衛軍官，他們在流放地維持學校、醫院與農場，進行地質與動植物考察，其中別斯特魯熱夫—留明兄弟與托爾所參與的北極圈探險，成為十九世紀俄羅斯科學史上最早的系統性探險之一；西伯利亞當地居民與商戶對這些拒絕向尼古拉一世宣誓的將軍相當歡迎。長期政治影響更為深遠：流放者留下的回憶、文稿以及在 1860 年代改革時期被重新發現的綱要，使十二月黨人成為俄國自由派與後來革命派的先驅象徵；在十九世紀末與二十世紀初的知識界，這批人的形象被反覆理想化，被視為被壓制的先知與啟蒙者。與此同時，帝國也從此確認，任何由軍官主導的政治集結都必須先摧毀其組織核心，於是秘密警察、軍事法庭與邊疆流放制度在往後數十年成為常態，而受壓制最直接的下層士兵則被投入高加索的戰事中消耗。
impactEn: The rising was crushed within a day, but the fissures it opened ran for half a century. Nicholas I's answer to surviving his throne was not liberalisation but contraction: the backbone of the secret societies were shipped in large numbers to Siberian places of confinement such as Nerchinsk, Chita and Petrovsky Zavod; the empire created the Third Section under Count Benckendorff to watch political dissent at home; the army was purged on a large scale; and about four thousand soldiers were formed into a combined guards regiment and sent to the Caucasian theatre, where they took part in the Russo-Turkish War of 1828 to 1829 and in the campaigns against the mountaineers of the Caucasus. Those men later became the emblem of every mutiny and every telling of the Decembrist story. The exiles themselves changed the eastern frontier: at Chita and Petrovsky Zavod gathered dozens of former guards officers with military and higher education, who kept schools, hospitals and farms in their places of exile and carried out geological and natural-historical surveys; the polar expedition in which the Bestuzhev-Ryumin brothers and Toll took part became one of the earliest systematic Russian scientific expeditions of the nineteenth century, and the local Siberian population and traders received these generals who had refused the oath to Nicholas I with marked hospitality. The long-term political effect was deeper still: the memoirs and papers of the exiles, and the programmes rediscovered during the reform decade of the 1860s, made the Decembrists a precursor symbol for Russian liberals and later revolutionaries, and in the intellectual world of the late nineteenth and early twentieth century their figure was idealised again and again as a suppressed prophet and an enlightener. At the same time the empire learned its lesson: any political gathering led by officers had to be broken at its organisational core first. Secret police, military courts and exile to the frontier became the standing instruments of the following decades, while the rank-and-file soldiers who bore the heaviest repression were consumed in the Caucasian wars.
result: 1825 年 12 月 26 日的元老院廣場起義以失敗告終。叛軍沒有奪取元老院、沒有奪取冬宮、沒有讓任何整團以上的駐軍倒戈；忠方用整日談判拖住叛軍，等候忠誠部隊集結，最後以近衛騎士團的騎兵衝鋒與三門野戰砲的葡萄彈齊射，把廣場上密集列隊的叛軍一次打散，退往結冰涅瓦河的殘部在砲火下再度被擊中而崩潰，起義在一天之內終結。元老院廣場的對峙很快延伸到南方：佩斯捷爾在事發前一天已被捕，南方社失去領袖，烏克蘭的切爾尼戈夫團與瓦西爾基夫駐軍在穆拉維約夫-阿波斯托爾率領下起事，卻因缺少足以對抗火砲的兵力，在五天內被平定，逾三千人受審或被捕。司法清算的結果寫在特別法庭與最高刑庭的記錄裡：北方社六十一人、南方社三十七人、聯合斯拉夫人二十三人受審，判刑最高至死刑與終身苦役，五名首要人物被處死，數十名骨幹被流放西伯利亞，士兵與下級軍官則受鞭刑、降級並被派往高加索。結果是雙面的：就當日而言，新皇尼古拉一世穩坐王位，帝國的專制統治得以延續；就長期而言，改革訴求並未消失，而是被推入地下，直到十九世紀六十年代才以另一種形式重新出現。
resultEn: The rising in Senate Square on 26 December 1825 ended in failure. The rebels took neither the Senate nor the Winter Palace, and no whole regiment of the garrison came over to them. The loyal side held the insurgents at bay through a day of negotiation while loyal units closed in, and then broke the densely ranked rebels in the square in a single stroke with the charge of the Chevalier Guard and the grapeshot of three field guns; the remnants who withdrew towards the frozen Neva were hit again by the guns and came apart, and the revolt was over within a single day. The confrontation in Senate Square was quickly echoed in the south: Pestel had already been arrested the day before, the Southern Society lost its leader, and the Chernigov Regiment and the Vasilkov garrison under Muravyov-Apostol rose in Ukraine, only to be put down within five days for want of any force that could stand up to artillery, with more than three thousand people arrested or brought to trial. The reckoning is written into the records of the special commissions and the Supreme Criminal Court: sixty-one of the Northern Society, thirty-seven of the Southern Society and twenty-three of the United Slavs were tried, with sentences running up to death and lifelong hard labour, five principal leaders put to death, dozens from the backbone of the societies sent to Siberia, and the soldiers and junior officers flogged, demoted and posted to the Caucasus. The outcome cuts both ways. In the moment, the new tsar Nicholas I sat securely on his throne and the autocratic order of the empire was preserved. In the longer run, the demand for reform did not disappear but was driven underground, and did not return in another shape until the 1860s.
